sections.overview: Native to Cuba and Hispaniola, this gecko has also established introduced populations in Florida. Its range differs from that of its congener Sphaerodactylus fantasticus, native to the Lesser Antilles.
sections.identification: The Reptile Database treats the Cuban and Hispaniolan populations as distinct named subspecies.
sections.habitat: Florida records place it around buildings, beneath bark and in moist ground debris or rotting logs.
sections.diet: A Florida field account recorded ants and a fly in the stomach of one female; this is a limited observation, not a full diet study.
sections.behavior: It uses small sheltered spaces at ground level and has also been found on human-made structures.
sections.ecology: Florida populations are non-native and were first recorded on Key West in the early twentieth century.
sections.conservation: The sources consulted document an established Florida introduction but do not provide a current global conservation category.

sources.title: A Runaway Train in the Making: Exotic Herpetofauna of Florida
